claim: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerases (PARPs) are a family of enzymes that synthesise ADP-ribosylation (ADPr), a reversible modification of proteins that regulates many different cellular processes.
source: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerases (PARPs) are a family of enzymes that synthesise ADP-ribosylation (ADPr), a reversible modification of proteins that regulates many different cellular processes.
evidence: This is a general statement about PARPs that draws from established scientific consensus in the field.

claim: Several mammalian PARPs are known to regulate the DNA damage response.
source: Several mammalian PARPs are known to regulate the DNA damage response, but it is not clear which amino acids in proteins are the primary ADPr targets.
evidence: This statement reflects established knowledge in the field about PARP function.

claim: ARH3 reverses the newly discovered type of ADPr (ADPr on serine residues; Ser-ADPr).
source: Previously, we reported that ARH3 reverses the newly discovered type of ADPr (ADPr on serine residues; Ser-ADPr) and developed tools to analyse this modification (Fontana et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: Ser-ADPr represents the major fraction of ADPr synthesised after DNA damage in mammalian cells.
source: Here, we show that Ser-ADPr represents the major fraction of ADPr synthesised after DNA damage in mammalian cells and that globally Ser-ADPr is dependent on HPF1, PARP1 and ARH3.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Globally Ser-ADPr is dependent on HPF1, PARP1 and ARH3.
source: Here, we show that Ser-ADPr represents the major fraction of ADPr synthesised after DNA damage in mammalian cells and that globally Ser-ADPr is dependent on HPF1, PARP1 and ARH3.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from knockout cell lines shown in the figures.

claim: In the absence of HPF1, glutamate/aspartate becomes the main target residues for ADPr.
source: In the absence of HPF1, glutamate/aspartate becomes the main target residues for ADPr.
evidence: This claim is supported by hydroxylamine treatment experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Serine is the primary form of ADPr in DNA damage signalling.
source: Our study establishes serine as the primary form of ADPr in DNA damage signalling.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by multiple experimental approaches.

claim: ADP-ribosylation (ADPr) is a reversible evolutionarily conserved posttranslational modification of proteins, which controls many critical cellular processes.
source: ADP-ribosylation (ADPr) is a reversible evolutionarily conserved posttranslational modification of proteins, which controls many critical cellular processes (Palazzo et al., 2017a; Lüscher et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerases (PARPs) compose the major family of enzymes that catalyse the transfer of ADP-ribose unit(s) from NAD+ to protein substrates.
source: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerases (PARPs) compose the major family of enzymes that catalyse the transfer of ADP-ribose unit(s) from NAD+ to protein substrates (Barkauskaite et al., 2015; Gupte et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Seventeen members of the PARP superfamily are encoded within the human genome.
source: Seventeen members of the PARP superfamily are encoded within the human genome, which are characterized by distinct structural domains, activities and involvement in a variety of cellular processes, including the DNA damage response (DDR) (Gupte et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: PARPs directly involved in DNA repair are PARP1, PARP2, and PARP3.
source: PARPs directly involved in DNA repair are PARP1, PARP2, and PARP3 (Langelier and Pascal, 2013; Martin-Hernandez et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: PARP3 can attach only a single ADP-ribose unit on target proteins (MARylation).
source: While PARP3 can attach only a single ADP-ribose unit on target proteins (MARylation) (Vyas et al., 2014), PARP1 and PARP2 can extend the initial ADPr event into long chains that remain attached on the proteins (Poly(ADP-ribosyl)ation, PARylation) (D'Amours et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: PARP1 and PARP2 can extend the initial ADPr event into long chains that remain attached on the proteins (Poly(ADP-ribosyl)ation, PARylation).
source: While PARP3 can attach only a single ADP-ribose unit on target proteins (MARylation) (Vyas et al., 2014), PARP1 and PARP2 can extend the initial ADPr event into long chains that remain attached on the proteins (Poly(ADP-ribosyl)ation, PARylation) (D'Amours et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: PARP-dependent ADPr of proteins is induced by binding of PARPs to DNA breaks.
source: PARP-dependent ADPr of these proteins is induced by binding of PARPs to DNA breaks, which produces timely and localised ADPr signals that control appropriate DDR mechanisms (Langelier et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: PARPs have previously been described to mainly target acidic residues (glutamates and aspartates; Glu and Asp, respectively) in proteins.
source: PARPs have previously been described to mainly target acidic residues (glutamates and aspartates; Glu and Asp, respectively) in proteins (Gagné et al., 2015; Daniels et al., 2015; Martello et al., 2016; Crawford et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Serine (Ser) residues are targets for PARP-dependent protein modification.
source: However, we recently showed that serine (Ser) residues are also targets for PARP-dependent protein modification (Leidecker et al., 2016; Crawford et al., 2018) and that Ser ADP-ribosylation (Ser-ADPr) is involved in processes underlying genome stability and the DDR, in particular (Bonfiglio et al., 2017a).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work by the authors.

claim: Ser ADP-ribosylation (Ser-ADPr) is involved in processes underlying genome stability and the DDR.
source: However, we recently showed that serine (Ser) residues are also targets for PARP-dependent protein modification (Leidecker et al., 2016; Crawford et al., 2018) and that Ser ADP-ribosylation (Ser-ADPr) is involved in processes underlying genome stability and the DDR, in particular (Bonfiglio et al., 2017a).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: The DNA damage responsive protein Histone PARylation Factor-1 (HPF1/C4orf27) forms complexes with either PARP1 or PARP2.
source: Furthermore, we showed that the DNA damage responsive protein Histone PARylation Factor-1 (HPF1/C4orf27) forms complexes with either PARP1 or PARP2 (Gibbs-Seymour et al., 2016) and promotes the synthesis of Ser-ADPr on a variety of protein substrates (Bonfiglio et al., 2017a).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: HPF1 promotes the synthesis of Ser-ADPr on a variety of protein substrates.
source: Furthermore, we showed that the DNA damage responsive protein Histone PARylation Factor-1 (HPF1/C4orf27) forms complexes with either PARP1 or PARP2 (Gibbs-Seymour et al., 2016) and promotes the synthesis of Ser-ADPr on a variety of protein substrates (Bonfiglio et al., 2017a).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: ARH3/ADPRHL2 is a hydrolase responsible for the specific reversal of Ser-ADPr in cells.
source: Finally, we discovered ARH3/ADPRHL2 as a hydrolase responsible for the specific reversal of Ser-ADPr in cells (Fontana et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: ADPr of proteins rapidly occurs to recruit and control activities of many crucial proteins involved in the repair of damaged DNA.
source: ADPr of proteins rapidly occurs to recruit and control activities of many crucial proteins involved in the repair of damaged DNA (Martin-Hernandez et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The study of ADPr has been significantly hampered by technical limitations, such as the barriers to visualize all forms of cellular ADPr and the challenges in proteomics analyses.
source: The study of ADPr has been significantly hampered by technical limitations, such as the barriers to visualize all forms of cellular ADPr and the challenges in proteomics analyses (Vivelo and Leung, 2015; Bonfiglio et al., 2017b).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Until recently, only anti-PAR antibodies have been available, which can detect only the long PAR chains.
source: For example, until recently, only anti-PAR antibodies have been available, which can detect only the long PAR chains.
evidence: This statement reflects established knowledge about available reagents in the field.

claim: A reagent specific for ADPr of any length (pan-ADPr antibody) as well as a reagent specific for mono-ADPr have been developed.
source: However, recently a reagent specific for ADPr of any length (referred here as a pan-ADPr antibody) as well as a reagent specific for mono-ADPr have been developed (Gibson et al., 2017) and allowed us to follow protein ADPr events in cells upon DNA damage.
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: In control U2OS cells, pan-ADPr signals after DNA damage revealed a number of modified proteins in the extract.
source: In control cells, pan-ADPr signals after DNA damage revealed a number of modified proteins in the extract.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The most easily identifiable pan-ADPr signals relate to the modification of histone proteins as well as PARP automodification.
source: The most easily identifiable signals relate to the modification of histone proteins as well as PARP automodification (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Both histone and PARP automodification signals can be recognised by the reagent that is specific for MARylation (mono-ADPr antibody).
source: Both signals can also be recognised by the reagent that is specific for MARylation (referred here as a mono-ADPr antibody; Figure 1A) (Gibson et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and citation to prior literature.

claim: 2 hr after DNA damage the global ADPr signal is reduced to the levels comparable to untreated cells.
source: 2 hr after DNA damage the global ADPr signal is reduced to the levels comparable to untreated cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The DNA damage-inducible ADPr is prevented in HPF1-depleted cells.
source: However, importantly, the DNA damage-inducible ADPr is prevented in HPF1-depleted cells (Figure 1A), as we observed previously for specific histone substrates (Bonfiglio et al., 2017a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and citation to prior work.

claim: The auto-modification of PARP1 is characterized by relatively longer ADPr chains (although also at overall lower levels) in HPF1-depleted cells when compared to control cells.
source: An exception is the auto-modification of PARP1 that is characterized by relatively longer ADPr chains (although also at overall lower levels) when compared to control cells (Figure 1A), as noted previously (Gibbs-Seymour et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and citation to prior work.

claim: Most of the global ADPr signal was abolished in PARP1 KO cells.
source: Expectedly, most of the global ADPr signal was abolished in PARP1 KO cells, as we showed previously for histone Ser-ADPr marks (Bonfiglio et al., 2017a), confirming that PARP1 is the most active PARP involved in DDR (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and citation to prior work.

claim: PARP1 is the most active PARP involved in DDR.
source: Expectedly, most of the global ADPr signal was abolished in PARP1 KO cells, as we showed previously for histone Ser-ADPr marks (Bonfiglio et al., 2017a), confirming that PARP1 is the most active PARP involved in DDR (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing loss of ADPr signal in PARP1 KO cells.

claim: Two independent clones of HPF1 KO cells showed comparable results regarding global ADPr dependence on HPF1.
source: In order to investigate whether the global pan-ADPr is truly dependent on HPF1, we tested two independent clones of HPF1 KO cells and observed comparable results with both cell lines (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Global ADPr in response to DNA damage requires both HPF1 and PARP1.
source: These data suggest that global ADPr in response to DNA damage requires both HPF1 and PARP1.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing loss of ADPr in both HPF1 and PARP1 KO cells.

claim: ARH3 KO cells showed notably higher levels of ADPr proteins under unstimulated conditions when compared to control cells.
source: As observed in our previous study (Fontana et al., 2017), ARH3 KO cells already showed notably higher levels of ADPr proteins under unstimulated conditions when compared to control cells (Figure 1A–B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1A-B and citation to prior work.

claim: The difference in ADPr signal upon DNA damage was much more pronounced in ARH3-deficient extracts and allowed detection of a number of additional ADP-ribosylated protein bands that persisted for at least 2 hr.
source: However, the difference in ADPr signal upon DNA damage was much more pronounced and allowed detection of a number of additional ADP-ribosylated protein bands in ARH3-deficient extracts that persisted for at least 2 hr.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1A-B.

claim: Histone ADPr detected by the pan-ADPr reagent was especially pronounced in ARH3-deficient extracts.
source: This was especially obvious for histone ADPr detected by the pan-ADPr reagent (Figure 1A–B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1A-B.

claim: MMS treatment results in ADPr signal that is consistent with H2O2 treatment observations.
source: Consistent with the observations for H2O2 treatment, most of the ADPr signal was HPF1-dependent and persisted in ARH3-deficient cells (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Most of the ADPr signal after MMS treatment was HPF1-dependent and persisted in ARH3-deficient cells.
source: Consistent with the observations for H2O2 treatment, most of the ADPr signal was HPF1-dependent and persisted in ARH3-deficient cells (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: HEK293 cells showed a number of ADP-ribosylated proteins detected by pan-ADPr antibody.
source: Notably, HEK293 cells showed a number of ADP-ribosylated proteins detected by pan-ADPr antibody and modifications of most of these proteins were strictly dependent on HPF1 protein (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Modifications of most ADP-ribosylated proteins in HEK293 cells were strictly dependent on HPF1 protein.
source: Notably, HEK293 cells showed a number of ADP-ribosylated proteins detected by pan-ADPr antibody and modifications of most of these proteins were strictly dependent on HPF1 protein (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The dependence of ADPr regulation on HPF1 and ARH3 suggests that Ser-ADPr is the dominant form of ADPr upon DNA damage.
source: The dependence of ADPr regulation on HPF1 and ARH3 suggests that Ser-ADPr is the dominant form of ADPr upon DNA damage.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing HPF1 and ARH3 dependence.

claim: Recent proteomic analyses capable of detecting Ser-ADPr are consistent with Ser-ADPr being the dominant form of ADPr upon DNA damage.
source: This is consistent with the data from recent proteomic analyses capable of detecting Ser-ADPr (Leidecker et al., 2016; Bonfiglio et al., 2017a; Bilan et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature including the authors' own work.

claim: Proteomics studies based on hydroxylamine, which excludes ADPr mapping on residues other than Glu and Asp, showed that modification of these residues is widespread in DDR.
source: However, proteomics studies based on hydroxylamine, which excludes ADPr mapping on residues other than the Glu and Asp (Moss et al., 1983; Daniels et al., 2015), showed that modification of these residues is widespread in DDR (Zhang et al., 2013; Gibson et al., 2017; Zhen et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Hydroxylamine does not remove ADPr from Ser residues.
source: Importantly, using defined substrates for both Ser-ADPr (Bonfiglio et al., 2017a; Fontana et al., 2017) and Glu/Asp-ADPr (Sharifi et al., 2013), we showed by autoradiography that hydroxylamine does not remove ADPr from Ser residues (Figure 2A) while confirming the complete removal of ADPr from Glu/Asp (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Hydroxylamine completely removes ADPr from Glu/Asp residues.
source: Importantly, using defined substrates for both Ser-ADPr (Bonfiglio et al., 2017a; Fontana et al., 2017) and Glu/Asp-ADPr (Sharifi et al., 2013), we showed by autoradiography that hydroxylamine does not remove ADPr from Ser residues (Figure 2A) while confirming the complete removal of ADPr from Glu/Asp (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: No noticeable loss of either the global ADPr or PARylation signal was observed after hydroxylamine treatment in DNA-damaged wild type cells.
source: We observed no noticeable loss of either the global ADPr or PARylation signal in DNA-damaged cells (Figure 2D) and only a moderate reduction in untreated cells (Figure 2C), indicating that under these conditions Glu/Asp-ADPr is not abundant.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Only a moderate reduction in ADPr signal was observed after hydroxylamine treatment in untreated wild type cells.
source: We observed no noticeable loss of either the global ADPr or PARylation signal in DNA-damaged cells (Figure 2D) and only a moderate reduction in untreated cells (Figure 2C), indicating that under these conditions Glu/Asp-ADPr is not abundant.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Under the experimental conditions, Glu/Asp-ADPr is not abundant in wild type cells.
source: We observed no noticeable loss of either the global ADPr or PARylation signal in DNA-damaged cells (Figure 2D) and only a moderate reduction in untreated cells (Figure 2C), indicating that under these conditions Glu/Asp-ADPr is not abundant.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the hydroxylamine treatment data showing minimal signal loss.

claim: Hydroxylamine completely abolished both the global ADPr and PAR signals on proteins extracted from HPF1 KO cells.
source: In contrast, intriguingly, hydroxylamine completely abolished both the global ADPr and PAR signals on proteins extracted from HPF1 KO cells (Figure 2C–D), implying that in the absence of HPF1 virtually all the ADPr is on acidic residues.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2C-D.

claim: In the absence of HPF1 virtually all the ADPr is on acidic residues.
source: In contrast, intriguingly, hydroxylamine completely abolished both the global ADPr and PAR signals on proteins extracted from HPF1 KO cells (Figure 2C–D), implying that in the absence of HPF1 virtually all the ADPr is on acidic residues.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the hydroxylamine treatment data showing complete signal loss in HPF1 KO cells.

claim: Asp and Glu are the prevalent target residues when in vitro ADPr reactions are performed without HPF1.
source: This cellular finding is in accordance with the well-established biochemical evidence that Asp and Glu are the prevalent target residues when in vitro ADPr reactions are performed without HPF1 (Tao et al., 2009; Sharifi et al., 2013; Bonfiglio et al., 2017a).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: H2B was identified by mass spectrometry to be ADP-ribosylated exclusively on Ser residues.
source: In our previous studies, we identified by mass spectrometry ADPr of H2B exclusively on Ser residues (Leidecker et al., 2016) and showed that this modification is highly dependent on HPF1 in cells (Bonfiglio et al., 2017a).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work by the authors.

claim: H2B modification is highly dependent on HPF1 in cells.
source: In our previous studies, we identified by mass spectrometry ADPr of H2B exclusively on Ser residues (Leidecker et al., 2016) and showed that this modification is highly dependent on HPF1 in cells (Bonfiglio et al., 2017a).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: The H2B S6A mutant did not show any ADPr in both control and HPF1-depleted cells.
source: In addition, the S6A mutant did not show any ADPr in both control and HPF1-depleted cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3A-B.

claim: Ser residue at position six is the main acceptor site of ADPr on H2B.
source: These data demonstrate that Ser residue at position six is the main acceptor site of ADPr on H2B (Leidecker et al., 2016) and confirm that this Ser-ADPr is HPF1-dependent (Bonfiglio et al., 2017a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the S6A mutant and citation to prior work.

claim: Ser-ADPr on H2B is HPF1-dependent.
source: These data demonstrate that Ser residue at position six is the main acceptor site of ADPr on H2B (Leidecker et al., 2016) and confirm that this Ser-ADPr is HPF1-dependent (Bonfiglio et al., 2017a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from HPF1 KO cells and citation to prior work.

claim: H3 ADPr sites in cells were detected on Ser10 and Ser28.
source: In our previous study, we detected H3 ADPr sites in cells on Ser10 and Ser28 (Leidecker et al., 2016), so we prepared the constructs for the expression of the Flag-tagged H3 wild type protein, the H3 alanine mutants at Ser10 (S10A) and Ser28 (S28A), as well as the double mutant (S10A S28A).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: The mutation of both Ser10 and Ser28 on H3 abolishes the DNA damage-induced H3 ADPr.
source: Flag-IP of the Flag-tagged proteins expressed in HEK293 cells and subsequent western blot against pan-ADPr revealed that the mutation of both Ser10 and Ser28 on H3 abolishes the DNA damage-induced H3 ADPr (Figure 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: ADPr predominantly happens on the Ser10 site of H3.
source: Furthermore, we observed that in our conditions ADPr predominantly happens on the Ser10 site, while the mutation of Ser28 showed a small, but significant reduction of ADPr.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The mutation of Ser28 on H3 showed a small, but significant reduction of ADPr.
source: Furthermore, we observed that in our conditions ADPr predominantly happens on the Ser10 site, while the mutation of Ser28 showed a small, but significant reduction of ADPr.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Expression of wild type and Ser-ADPr mutants in HEK293 cells should allow the validation of Ser-ADPr sites for many other ADP-ribosylated candidate proteins involved in the DDR.
source: In conclusion, the expression of wild type and Ser-ADPr mutants in HEK293 cells by this simple approach should allow the validation of Ser-ADPr sites for many other ADP-ribosylated candidate proteins involved in the DDR.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future applications of the method.

claim: Glu, Asp, Lys, Arg and Ser have been indicated as the major ADPr target residues by recent proteomics studies.
source: Glu, Asp, Lys, Arg and Ser have been indicated as the major ADPr target residues by recent proteomics studies, some of which, however, employ sub-optimal approaches that may lead to misassignment of ADPr specificities (Bonfiglio et al., 2017b).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Some proteomics studies employ sub-optimal approaches that may lead to misassignment of ADPr specificities.
source: Glu, Asp, Lys, Arg and Ser have been indicated as the major ADPr target residues by recent proteomics studies, some of which, however, employ sub-optimal approaches that may lead to misassignment of ADPr specificities (Bonfiglio et al., 2017b).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: The attention is currently shifting from mere identification of ADPr sites to the elucidation of the biological pathways in which a form of ADPr plays a major role.
source: Thus, the attention is currently shifting from mere identification of ADPr sites to the elucidation of the biological pathways in which a form of ADPr plays a major role (Gupte et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The discovery of Ser-ADPr in 2016 has fuelled the rapid progress in the field.
source: Our discovery of Ser-ADPr in 2016 has fuelled the rapid progress in the field, which has already resulted in the identification of the 'eraser' of Ser-ADPr (Fontana et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: Computational reanalysis of a published ADPr dataset showed that Ser-ADPr is a widespread modification.
source: Our computational reanalysis (Matic et al., 2012) of a published ADPr dataset (Martello et al., 2016); ProteomeXchange ID: PXD004245) showed that Ser-ADPr is a widespread modification (Bonfiglio et al., 2017a).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work by the authors.

claim: In endogenous wild type cells Ser-ADPr is the primary form of ADPr upon DNA damage.
source: Our findings show that in endogenous wild type cells Ser-ADPr is the primary form of ADPr upon DNA damage.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: An independent study using unbiased proteomics technology showed that the vast majority of ADPr localises on Ser residues.
source: This is consistent with the data from an independent study, in which an unbiased proteomics technology (Bonfiglio et al., 2017b) showed that the vast majority of ADPr localises on Ser residues (Bilan et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Asp and Glu are the main targets of ADPr in PARP1-dependent, but HPF1-independent DNA damage signalling.
source: Importantly, our data indicate that Asp and Glu are the main targets of ADPr in PARP1-dependent, but HPF1-independent DNA damage signalling.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from HPF1 KO cells treated with hydroxylamine.

claim: The data extend the concept of the 'switching' of PARP1 amino acid specificity to the cellular context.
source: This extends the concept of the 'switching' of PARP1 amino acid specificity (Bonfiglio et al., 2017a; Leung, 2017) to the cellular context.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature and inference from the experimental data.

claim: Future studies are needed to unravel the physiological and pathological conditions controlled by Ser-ADPr and Asp/Glu-ADPr.
source: Future studies are needed to unravel the physiological and pathological conditions controlled by Ser-ADPr and Asp/Glu-ADPr.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future research directions.

claim: The discovery of Ser-ADPr as well as the recent discoveries of reversible ADPr of DNA have added considerable depth to our understanding of the function and versatility of ADPr signalling in the cell.
source: In conclusion, the discovery of Ser-ADPr as well as the recent discoveries of reversible ADPr of DNA (Jankevicius et al., 2016; Talhaoui et al., 2016; Munnur and Ahel, 2017; Dölle and Ziegler, 2017) have added considerable depth to our understanding of the function and versatility of ADPr signalling in the cell, and raise the possibility that there may be other unique cellular and molecular processes regulated by ADPr.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: There may be other unique cellular and molecular processes regulated by ADPr.
source: In conclusion, the discovery of Ser-ADPr as well as the recent discoveries of reversible ADPr of DNA (Jankevicius et al., 2016; Talhaoui et al., 2016; Munnur and Ahel, 2017; Dölle and Ziegler, 2017) have added considerable depth to our understanding of the function and versatility of ADPr signalling in the cell, and raise the possibility that there may be other unique cellular and molecular processes regulated by ADPr.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future discoveries.
